doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: Young Tuxedo Band and the Island Queen riverboat
summary: Paul forms the Young Tuxedo Band, plays the Island Queen with Sidney's band, and discusses riverboats in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Well the Tuxedo original original tuxedo band we did pretty good but we had times we had a pretty rock we wasn't making anything. At one time I quit the band and I formed another band and the band was good and we called it the Young Tuxedo Band and we'd get work from them. I was always growing from band because I wasn't doing anything much. So I left that band and I went with Sidney Daysbeens band. We played out on the Island Queen, you see, around 25.
Well where did you go on that boat? We didn't go anywhere.
We just played over at the head of the, right the river. Right it was here.
I thought it was mostly up around Cincinnati and Ohio.
I never did go away with the boat.
No we played right there every night. Well did the Streckfus boat? But the boat would go up the river a piece. Yeah I know. And come by.
I didn't know they played here in New Orleans. I thought only the Streckfus boat played here most of the time. Like the St. Paul and Sidney and the JS and those boats.
I never played on that but I played on the President. See I played that boat.
In those days then when the Island Queen, that was a rival line, did they have two dances? I just kind of. I mean two boats here at the same time?

I just don't remember if they had two at the same time. But I know what we played, I played the Capitol on the Capitol and with Papa Solis there. Not regular, we played jobs on the Capitol. But I did play regular on the Island Queen in Sidney. And that was around 1925. But I didn't play it, stayed there too long. I left the band and went back with Papa Solis there and band and stayed there until 27.
I didn't know that, that bothers me about that boat being here. Was that winter time or summer?
In the cold weather when they played.
